reuse.why: The change reuses recurrence conversion and date adjustment helpers and shares holiday recognition, but repeats occurrence policy orchestration across consumers.

duplication.why: getDatesInRange repeats getUpcomingDates' daily exclusion and conditional business-day adjustment pipeline instead of sharing that transformation.

placement.why: Holiday matching and date movement belong in shared/schedules.ts, although the handlers retain some shared scheduling policy.

scope.why: The edits are focused on the requested scheduling rules, range handler, supporting configuration, tests and release note.

maintainability.why: The small helpers are understandable, but repeated occurrence transformations and separate lookahead and padding calculations make future scheduling changes harder to coordinate.

bypasses_abstraction.where: The changed consumers use the shared recurrence, daily-skip, holiday-recognition and date-adjustment helpers.

disguised_duplication.where: shared/schedules.ts:getNextDate selects a business day with find, while server/schedules/app.ts:getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange reshape the same exclusion policy into filters before conditional adjustment.

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains the holidays parameter and getNextDate gains a daily-skip branch; consumers continue using shared primitives, but the two handlers repeat their composition.
